provenance: legacy SemStreams capture; not a SemEngine result

constraints.rationale: Constructor is the standard constructor signature every service must follow, and Registry.Register is the one entry point that admits a named Constructor into the constructors map. Changing the signature or the registration rules (empty name, nil constructor, duplicate name) means reading both: the type defines what Register stores and Register defines how the type is catalogued.

RegisterAll is where the built-in service catalogue is named, and it binds the registry name "heartbeat" to NewHeartbeatService; NewHeartbeatService exists in the Constructor shape precisely so that binding compiles. Renaming the service, changing its constructor shape or making it opt-in requires both sides.

The package documentation's Metrics Integration section lists semstreams_startup_units as the Manager-owned startup observation with its admitted/invoked/completed/failed counts; newStartupMetricWriter is where that exact gauge (namespace semstreams, subsystem startup, name units, owner/stage labels) is built and registered. The passage documents this constructor's behaviour, so a change to the gauge's name, labels or stages has to be reflected in the doc.

resolveServiceConfigs materializes metrics as the default-on optional service with the raw JSON {"path":"/metrics","port":9090}, and NewMetrics is the constructor that decodes that JSON strictly (unknown fields rejected) and applies the same 9090 and /metrics defaults for zero values. The default activation of the metrics service is split across these two functions; a change to the materialized JSON keys or defaults must agree with what NewMetrics accepts.

HTTPHandler is the optional interface a service implements to expose HTTP endpoints (RegisterHTTPHandlers plus OpenAPISpec), and StorageObservabilityService.RegisterHTTPHandlers is one of its implementations, pinned by the compile-time assertion at line 51. Anyone changing the interface's prefix/mux contract needs this implementer, and anyone changing how the report route mounts needs the contract it satisfies.

Configurable's own comment says the Metrics service is currently its only implementer, and Metrics.ConfigSchema states that it implements Configurable for UI discovery. The interface and its sole implementation carry one responsibility, service configuration discovery; the interface is unreachable in this family without the method and the method is meaningless without the interface.

OpenAPISpec carries ResponseTypes and RequestBodyTypes as reflect.Type lists that are explicitly 'to generate schemas for', and SchemaFromType is the reflect.Type to JSON Schema generator that turns those into the components/schemas entries a ResponseSpec.SchemaRef points at. The spec fragment supplies the types and the schema generator produces their definitions; one is incomplete without the other.

ManagerConfig exposes the API metadata block as server_info typed InfoSpec, the same struct OpenAPIDocument carries as its info section. The operator-configured title, description and version flow from the manager config into the served document through this one type, so adding or renaming an InfoSpec field changes the configuration surface too.

deliveryFatalReporter exists only so that MilestoneService.Health can assert it on the subscriber and turn a latched DeliveryFatal error into an unhealthy verdict; the interface comment explains why it is asserted rather than folded into milestoneStarter. The health read and the seam it reads through are one responsibility.

ProjectionBinder declares the three methods a rule processor offers for projection wiring, and preflightRulePackMutations is the pass that drives two of them (PreflightProjectionMutations, then ProjectionBindings) and validates pack IDs, duplicates and contracts before any client is injected. The interface's contract that contracts are validated before injection is implemented by this function.

Both are small Config structs with a port field and the identical header comment 'Simple struct - no UnmarshalJSON, no Enabled field', so they read as two copies of one thing. MetricsConfig configures the Prometheus metrics listener (port 9090, path) of the metrics service; ManagerConfig configures the Manager's main HTTP server, Swagger UI, API info and read/write timeouts. Grouping them conflates two different servers.

Same method name, same value receiver on a *Config struct and the same doc comment 'Validate checks if the configuration is valid', the boilerplate every service config repeats. One parses and bounds the heartbeat log interval; the other delegates to logforwarderpolicy to check the NATS log forwarding min_level and exclude_sources. They validate unrelated settings for unrelated services.

Both are 'Register' calls that store a value under a service name in a map guarded by a sync.RWMutex, so the shape and the word registry match exactly. Registry.Register admits a service Constructor so the Manager can compose services; RegisterOpenAPISpec stores an OpenAPI fragment from init() for the openapi-generator tool. One is boot composition, the other documentation generation.

Both build a 'schema' object from a properties map plus a required list, so they share the term and the shape. NewConfigSchema produces the component-style ConfigSchema a service exposes through Configurable for UI discovery of its configuration; schemaFromStruct produces JSON Schema for the OpenAPI components of HTTP response and request body types by reflection. Config-discovery schema and OpenAPI JSON Schema are different documents for different readers.

The two Stop methods are near line-for-line copies of one lifecycle scaffold: a startDone wait loop, the used/stopping/terminal/cleanupPending flags and the same 'concurrent Stop is unsupported' error. Beneath the scaffold they tear down unrelated things, the Prometheus metrics HTTP server versus the agent-run milestone JetStream consumers, so a grouping driven by the shared boilerplate would join two services that never touch each other.

Both bring up an operator diagnostic HTTP listener on a configured port and log 'Starting ... server', which makes them look like two instances of the same start routine. pprof.go explains at length that pprof is deliberately not a Service: fire-and-forget, started before NATS, no Stop, bind failure never a boot gate. Metrics.Start is a lifecycle-managed Service start with rollback on failure, health reporting and a Manager-claimed mode. Grouping them would undo exactly the distinction the pprof comment draws.

Both are GET-only JSON handlers with the identical scaffold: reject non-GET with 405 'Method not allowed', set Content-Type application/json, json.NewEncoder(w).Encode and log an encode failure. serveGraphTriples parses triple filters and scans the ENTITY_STATES KV bucket through the Manager; handleReport projects the consumed storage capacity report snapshot with no I/O. Graph read endpoint and storage report endpoint share only the net/http boilerplate.

Both are the same ticker loop: emit once on entry, then select on ctx.Done and ticker.C and emit on each tick. heartbeatLoop logs a debug system heartbeat (uptime, goroutines, component health counts) for the heartbeat service; run re-evaluates stream migration override expiry against live config, setting a gauge and warning per lapsed bridge. Periodic shape is shared, the subject (liveness log versus stream hygiene reporting) is not.

Two unexported helper methods with the same name and the same shape, register(target), on small reporter/surface structs. One registers a Prometheus GaugeVec with the metrics registrar for the override-expiry series; the other mounts the storage report HTTP route on the mux under the service prefix. Metrics registration and HTTP route registration are different planes, and the shared name is the only likeness.

Both classify a change into a small vocabulary of operation strings, create/update/delete versus add/enable/disable/remove/reconfigure, so a reader sees two change-detection classifiers. detectKVOperation labels one NATS KV entry for the message-logger SSE watch stream; pendingServiceChanges diffs the boot service composition against desired config to report restart-required changes. KV watch events and service composition drift are unrelated subjects.
